title.rendered: Declaring Over Your Provision: My God Shall Supply | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 10

excerpt.rendered: God is not a sponsor; He is a Father. Day 10 teaches believers how to declare over finances from Philippians 4:19 and Deuteronomy 8:18.

content.rendered:
God is not a sponsor; He is a Father. And a Father promises His supply, not merely His presence, over every need His children carry.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, October 27, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 10

Today’s Scripture

“And my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus.”
Philippians 4:19 (NKJV)

“And you shall remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you power to get wealth, that He may establish His covenant which He swore to your fathers, as it is this day.”
Deuteronomy 8:18 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Philippians 4:19 is a sentence many believers quote and few believers rest in. The NKJV says, “my God shall supply all your need.” The AMPC says, “And my God will liberally supply (fill to the full) your every need.” The TPT says, “I am convinced that my God will fully satisfy every need you have, for I have seen the abundant riches of glory revealed to me through the Anointed One, Jesus Christ.” Deuteronomy 8:18 completes the picture: God is the one who gives His people power to get wealth, and He does it to establish His covenant.

From Lagos to London, Manila to Nairobi to São Paulo, believers are learning that provision is not a prosperity gospel and it is not a poverty gospel. It is a covenant gospel. God promises enough. God promises to supply. God promises to teach His people to work, invest, save, and give. In the compound, in the office, in the market, in the online store, in the ministry, the believer declares, “My God shall supply all my need.” Not greed. Not fantasy. Need, and need according to His riches in glory.

Jesus modelled this often. He paid taxes from a fish’s mouth (Matthew 17:27). He fed thousands from a small boy’s lunch (John 6). He told His disciples to look at the birds and the lilies, and to seek first the kingdom (Matthew 6:33). He taught them to pray, “Give us this day our daily bread.” And He never apologised for mentioning money. He understood that stewardship is spiritual, and that a mouth filled with faith will eventually have hands filled with harvest.

So declare it with reverence and gratitude. Tithe. Give. Plan. Work hard. Pursue skill. And over every project and every month and every account, open your mouth and agree with Scripture: My God shall supply. He gives me power to get wealth. He is faithful to establish His covenant.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. God promises supply, not sponsorship. He fills needs, teaches wealth, and establishes covenant. Everything begins at that door.

Personalise. Name your real needs. School fees. Rent. A plane ticket. Business capital. Medical bills. Ministry projects. Faith is specific; vague prayer breeds vague answers.

Proclaim. Speak Philippians 4:19 by name over each need. Thank God for the harvest already assigned to you. Confess that He is teaching your hands to work and your heart to steward.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that my God shall supply all my need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus. I am not an orphan hunting for crumbs. I am a child of the Most High, and my Father is faithful. He gives me power to get wealth that He may establish His covenant. My work is blessed. My skill is sharpened. My savings grow. My giving is sanctified. My debts are being settled. My business doors open at the voice of the Lord. I will not be anxious about tomorrow, because tomorrow’s bread is already on my Father’s table. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
